summary: The packet defines strong fail-closed scanning, artifact validation, verification, and framework boundaries, but the raw-ARIA fallback does not enforce its documented DNS-drift boundary and the preflight launcher validates its interpreter against the bundle location rather than the target project.

findings.title: Raw-ARIA navigation is not pinned to the approved DNS snapshot
findings.evidence: The request guard performs only URL-origin validation and then calls route.continue(); assertSafeNavigation accepts the hostname localhost but neither resolves it nor compares its address with the preflight snapshot. This contradicts the documented requirement to reject address-snapshot drift before emitting a snapshot and permits a changed localhost resolution to receive browser traffic after preflight.
findings.recommendation: Pass the approved peer snapshot into the helper and enforce it at the browser transport boundary, or restrict this fallback to canonical numeric loopback literals and fail closed for localhost.

findings.title: Interpreter exclusion uses the bundle root instead of the target project
findings.evidence: project_root is derived by walking three parents from the launcher directory. The subsequent interpreter check therefore excludes the skill bundle's ancestor, not the current target project promised by the public contract.
findings.recommendation: Resolve and validate the approved target-project root independently, then reject interpreter paths beneath that root while retaining the bundle-identity checks.

findings.title: Output template requests a raw artifact error
findings.evidence: The finding template labels the error as a raw error message, while the artifact reader contract requires redaction and bounded projections before output and the safety section treats report text as untrusted.
findings.recommendation: Change the field to a quoted, sanitized reader projection and explicitly forbid substituting directly read artifact text.

limitations: Packet-only static review; no commands, tests, benchmarks, network checks, or runtime probes were performed.
Omitted holdouts, scorecards, benchmark results, CI dependencies, repository history, and non-selected product surfaces were not assessed.
This is not full product coverage, skill-accuracy measurement, independent ground truth, human or sealed review, or remote model attestation.
